newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols stage modest recovery.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols stage modest recovery.

text.p: Implied volatilities for options on U.S. Treasury bond futures notched higher for a second straight day, a noteworthy bounce given their protracted slump, options traders said.
June volatility climbed to 8.70 percent late in the session Tuesday from about 8.50 percent at Monday's settlement, while September gained 0.1 point to 9.23 percent.
June's value, at less than 9.00 percent, remains quite low, floor traders emphasized. Volatility buyers may suspect the downtrend has simply run out of steam, they said.
"Historically, it is incredibly low to be in the eight percent area," said one bond floor trader for a U.S. banking firm.

Interest rate options traders are also beginning to look ahead to next week's heavy lineup of U.S. economic data. Highlights include the employment cost index on Tuesday, gross domestic product on Wednesday and employment on Friday.
Despite their sideways trading pattern, bond futures have staged some sharp swings within the ranges of the past few sessions, contributing to the upswing in volatility, said the bond floor trader.

Helping to boost volatility was a large calendar spread involving the purchase of 5,000 September 112-00 bond calls against sales in the June calls, floor sources said. Buying the September 112-00 calls and selling the June 112-00 calls may reflect an opinion that futures prices will remain below the strike through the May 16 expiration of June options, then rally before the September options expire in mid-August.
Floor traders said activity turned brisk in late morning while bond futures edged mildly higher, but options trades had a bearish slant, favoring put purchases and call selling.

Other notable bearish transactions included a Wall Street dealer's firm packaged purchase of 2,000 June 105-00/106-00 bond put spreads and sale of 2,000 June 110-00 calls. Another dealer bought 3,000 September 104-00 puts.

Implied volatilities for Eurodollar options also gained, helped by active buying of short-dated June 93.00 puts, a floor broker at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. One house picked up 4,000 of the options early in the day, setting the tone for the session.

Volatility for short-dated June midcurve options rose 0.3 point to 16.00 percent, while September midcurves gained 0.6 point, climbing to 16.30 percent. Midcurve options expire in 1997 but are priced from 1998 futures.
Quarterly options volatility increased to 10.70 percent in September, up 0.2 point on the day, and to 12.30 percent in December, a gain of 0.3 point.
